Subject: Stakeholder mapping & procurement next steps - Aurora Retail

Hi Sophie —

Great to meet the team earlier today. Thanks again for the demo slot and for walking us through Aurora's priorities for Q3 (improving customer support automation and reducing per-conversation MTTR).

Quick recap and asks so we can align next steps: 
- Primary desired outcomes: lower latency for customer-facing assistants, enforce data residency controls for EU customers, and predictable monthly unit economics.
- Technical stakeholders that would need to review: Engineering (runtime + infra), Security/Privacy, and Platform/Integrations. Procurement/legal will handle T&Cs and SOC2 evidence.

Could you share a short stakeholder map or org chart that shows the decision owners for each of these areas (economic buyer, security/compliance lead, procurement contact, and the primary engineering lead)? A simple XLS or PDF is perfect. Also please include any procurement timelines (e.g., PO lead times, quarter close dates) so we can time a pilot.

I'll loop in Rishi from our solutions team — he'll prepare a tailored procurement checklist (SOC2 artifacts, data flow diagram, SLAs) and a short pricing estimate for a 3-month pilot.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share org chart + any procurement timing (by end of week)
2) Rishi to send procurement checklist & pilot quote (by Wed 6/18)
3) Quick sync with security + procurement if requested (30–45m)

Thanks — looking forward to partnering.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. I attached a first-pass org chart (see aurora-org-chart-v1.xlsx) — informal but should show the main owners. A few notes: 
- Economic buyer: Rajesh Patel (VP Product) — cc'd on this thread.
- Security/compliance: Priya Natarajan (Head of InfoSec) — she prefers to review questionnaires but will usually ask for SOC2, pen test report, and a data flow diagram.
- Procurement: Laura Bennett (Director, Procurement) — PO usually takes 2–3 weeks once legal signs off.

Timeline: We're aiming to decide on a pilot by the end of July to run during August. Procurement will need a pricing estimate and the SOC2 evidence to start the legal review.

I'll loop Rajesh into the thread. Happy to jump on a quick sync if helpful.

Best,

Thanks Sophie and Marissa —

Marissa, good to meet you. Quick clarifications from my side:
- Our primary metric for choosing a vendor is predictable per-conversation cost at scale (we run ~200k conv/month) while meeting 95th percentile latency < 400ms for end-user responses.
- We need the ability to run a private deployment for EU customer data (VPC or dedicated capacity) — can you confirm Redwood supports that and whether the pilot can be run in a dedicated bucket?
- Procurement: Laura will own the PO, but legal will want a standard review of indemnities; I can expedite once SOC2 + basic infosec pack is provided.

I'll be available next Tue afternoon for a quick 30m to review the procurement checklist.

Regards,
Rajesh Patel
VP Product | Aurora Retail
rajesh.patel@aurora-retail.com

Hi all —

Thanks for the details and the org chart, Sophie. Marissa looped me in — attaching a concise procurement & security checklist that covers the common asks: SOC2 report, pen test summary, data flow diagram, encryption/KMS options, SLA targets, and sample contract redlines.

Quick answers to Rajesh's questions:
- Yes — we support private deployments (VPC) and dedicated capacity; pilots can be scoped for a dedicated pool for EU data. I'll include two pricing options in the pilot quote (hosted pilot vs. dedicated pilot) with ballpark MRR for a three-month trial.
- For latency: we target configurable 95th-percentile SLAs; I'll include measured latency examples from comparable retail customers.

Next from us:
1) I'll send the procurement checklist + two pilot pricing options by end of day Wednesday (6/18).
2) Marissa — do you want me to prepare a short security slide deck for Priya ahead of a sync?
